No stray `habits.json` was ever created (the `rm -f` found nothing to remove); the test files correctly point at temp files.

**What changed:** `habit done <name> [when]` now accepts an optional trailing date — `today`, `yesterday`, or `YYYY-MM-DD` — parsed by a new `parseDateArg()` in `src/streak.js` and wired up in `src/cli.js`; `src/commands.js` is untouched since its `done(name, today)` signature already took a specific `Date`. Added unit tests for `parseDateArg` and an end-to-end CLI test; all 13 tests pass.

**One thing to decide:** since habit names can contain spaces, a habit literally named `yesterday` or a plain ISO date would be misread as a date argument instead of a name (e.g. `habit done yesterday` marks a habit named `""`). I picked the simple heuristic (trailing token matching a date pattern) since it matches exactly what you asked for; let me know if you'd rather require a flag like `--on yesterday` to avoid that edge case.
